Prove or falsify this REPAIRED complete last-stage algorithm. This is a new finite-etale-order mechanism after the completed orbit report correctly falsified direct reduction under p-scaled encoding; do not repeat candidate searches for good target encodings. Native ultimate task smooth quintic/F_p full P2; current isolated question reconstruct actual Galois-stable finite torsion group and arithmetic Frobenius in poly(ell,B=logp), all rank/n/r fixed. No tools, browsing or new source claims. Give an actual final proof/obstruction before budget exhaustion.

Inputs are explicit and remain conditional: genuine full constant-Gamma frame cover from original family, Gamma=GSp_n(Fell), all plane/function-field/model/deck sizes polyell,B; geometrically components smooth. Curve has good abstract reduction at TARGET p and a faithful explicitly constructible good model at SMALL AUXILIARY P. Natural Gamma-submodule E of product Jacobian ell-torsion has fixed rank R (either full natural socle n*(r-2)n, or separately supplied genuine parabolic socle rank n*(r-2n)); E globally Galois-stable. Small-P algorithm supplies ALL E and exact operations over one extension of polynomial degree, then unique numerical ell-torsion lifts to any charged precision. Support and CLOSED divisor A,B,C encoding height theorem is established: polyell,B uniformly for all E when a common basepoint is chosen with residue h0=1 and outside polyell chart exceptions; all jet/eta/Vandermonde terms paid, not just x-values. Explicit plane F and field presentations for LOCAL lifting paid; no global torsion field or Galois labels supplied. Target unramifiedness of E and of the regular frame fibre is an input here, not good-coordinate reduction.

Parent construction:
1. Choose rational a=a0+p*k, where a0 modp avoids native branch (fixedr), k in 0..L with L a known polynomial bound for images of bad basepoints (uniqueness, pole/chart avoidance for all E on all components) at auxiliary P. Choose P>L+2, P!=p, P>2g-1, avoiding explicit model/RR certificate; numerical P still polyell,B. Then the candidates are distinct modulo P and one works; test all b over the fibre and all classes by closed RR. This ensures good canonical extraction at P and char0, while target b-torsor unramified. loga=O(B+logL). Regular FULL Gamma torsor fibre has all points in ONE residue field of degree<=|Gamma| (can take degree|Gamma|); combine with already-paid universal E field/evaluation extension by a bounded product, not arbitrary factor lcm.
2. Encode ALL pairs S=B_a×E using b coordinates and, for ALL g in Gamma, canonical closed divisors for the component of R_g b with class t_component. Components represented with genuine deck descent, include cyclotomic coordinate; all tuples are Galois-equivariant, no arbitrary component label/embedding. A class t is in actual E, not Hom multiplicity W. Count N=|Gamma| ell^R, polynomialell. Every scalar coordinate intrinsic height H polynomialell,B; b heights from plane roots at a. Their global field has degree<=|Gamma|*|GL_R(Fell)| but DO NOT construct it.
3. At P choose a common z=x+c y encoding each divisor by A,B,C with eta=F_y-cF_x unit and cyclicity, then choose moment-curve gamma=sum_j u^j enc_j separating all N pair tuples MOD P. Increase numerical P beforehand above the known polynomial bad-u and bad-c count; all coefficient choices polynomial bit size. P-adic Vandermonde is a unit. Canonical divisor algebra can be obtained from high-degree RR sections with pole divisor A=k*pi^-1(infinity), deg(A-E)>=2g, common section zeros exactly E. Clear normalization denominators and avoid their finite zeros via the basepoint bad set; fixed-variable ideal/Macaulay algebra or residue-pivot linear algebra yields the degree-g closed quotient without support splitting. All torsion+point lifts unique and compatible.
4. Form Q(X)=product_(s in S)(X-gamma_s), coordinate tables, zero-projector z0(b,t)=(b,0), addition ((b,t),(c,u))->(b,t+u), deck on b, actual deck on t, inversion/scalars, and the equivalence relation s~s' iff they have same t (ignoring b). These are all Galois-equivariant; interpolation over all labels gives RATIONAL coefficients. Bound all heights explicitly by polynomial in N,L,H,log coefficients, via Lagrange/Cramer; no arbitrary-field-basis height issue for rational invariants. Choose certified P precision from height bound; all denominators P units thanks modular separation. Rational reconstruction gives exact finite etale A_Q=Q^S with all operation tables. No guessed minimal polynomial/LLL, no support or global torsion splitting.
5. Take quotient finite set E via invariants constant on equivalence relation (linear equalities in A, or equalizer of two algebra maps from relation algebra; must construct relation table/idempotent without secretly knowing global labels). Need explicit polynomial Q-linear linear algebra, preserve genuine group/deck structure. Alternatively p-maximalize full S first then quotient finite-etale groupoid. Full degreeN polynomial eitherway.
6. Build integral order by scaling rational basis (including1) common structure denominators. Buchmann-Lenstra ACTUAL Algorithm6.1/Prop6.2 supplied: known-prime p-maximal overorder in polynomial(input bit,rank,logp), nilradical kernel x->x^(p^t) for p^t>rank, idealizer iteration at most discriminant valuation/2, original-order HNF bounds all intermediate bits. No p>rank or integer factoring required. Since A_Q unramified atp, final order localizedZp is finite etale. All Q-algebra operation maps extend to finite-etale orders/tensors. Reducing produces true finite E-set/group with Frobenius x->x^p even if gamma or canonical encodings collide targetp. This repairs Q=X(X-p) exactly; do not assume disc originalQ unit.
7. Recover Frobenius matrix on E without global labels: factor residue algebra and take ONE splitting field extension of bounded degree (Frob on R-dimensional E order<=|GL_R|; no lcm across unrelated factors). Evaluate operation maps on all geometric points, find F_ell basis by exhaustive bounded dimension R linear operations, express sigma_p using powering. Compute W=Hom_Gamma(Ndual,E) by deck-generator linear equations, with convention phi g^T=P(g)phi. Restrict to correctly supplied parabolic E if present. Unknown basis conjugation harmless; no arbitrary scalar because actual frame evaluation input. Arithmetic correction p^-2 gives H1(U,R1Fell); geometric inverse. Final surface assembly separate.

Try to falsify: selecting a before P vs after, all-component Galois encoding, canonical zero divisor gb meets forbidden poles, free field presentation, Galois equivariance of relation/group operations, obtaining closed quotient from RR, P-unit interpolation, p-max order map extension, and extracting actual matrix rather than permutation up to unknown twist. Admit only independently deduced bridges. Return complete conditional algorithm or smallest unclosed step with explicit counterexample; no full native match or quantum advantage claim.

# Canonical torsion-divisor support heights

2026-11-12. Parent derivation independently checked in
audits/reviews/2026-11-12-torsion-height-{finite,analytic}-chain.md; both full
reviews were parent-read. The completed OpenAI contraction report independently
obtained the graph bound. This proves the scoped support-VALUE height theorem
below, not a closed encoding or native surface algorithm. The direct broad
paid book-height request was empty. Retain the book signs and minimality guard.

## Input and proved bound

Let pi:C->P1 be a degree-d cover over Qbar, smooth connected C of genus
g>=1, with fixed total branch orbit <=r and logarithmic branch height hB.
Let T be N degree-zero torsion classes. Choose b over a SMALL NONZERO
INTEGER a outside branch/exceptional values such that every D_t in |t+gb|
is unique and avoids the poles of pi. All divisors are closed; field
extensions below are existential for normalized height bounds, not a
common splitting-field algorithm. Set S_N=d+1+hB+log(N+1). If A additional
geometric points must be avoided, replace log(N+1) by log(N(A+1)+1).

The lemmas below establish:

    sum_(Q with multiplicity in D_t) h(pi(Q)) <= C_r*d^9*S_N.

The exponent is deliberately loose. A supplied plane-model coordinate y
can then be charged using its equation F(pi,y)=0 and its coefficient
height H: h(y(Q))<=poly(deg F)*(H+h(pi(Q))+1), away from the finitely many
places requiring a different affine/normalization chart. Avoiding those
places is a separate finite bad-basepoint condition. A full closed-divisor
encoding still needs a precise primitive-coordinate/jet reconstruction
argument; a polynomial for pi-values alone can lose branch labels.

## Finite model-transfer lemma

Let Z be the regular semistable cover-compatible model from the reviewed
Javanpeykar construction, with pi a MORPHISM to P1 over the integers.
Let f:Z->Y contract to the relatively minimal regular semistable model.
Work after finite extension so horizontal supports and components split.
Every contraction is a rational (-1) tail, inverse to blowing up a smooth
point; blowing up a node would introduce a multiplicity-two component.

For a section b define L_s(b) as the number of smooth blowup centres traversed
by its successive images. Each contributes one. Then

    sum_s L_s(b) log Norm(s) / [K:Q]
       = h_Z(b)-h_Y(b) <= h_Z(b),

by omega_Z=f^*omega_Y+exceptional contributions, identical archimedean
metrics, and nonnegativity of stable Arakelov point height. For every
distinct section P,

    I_Y,s(b,P) <= I_Z,s(b,P)+L_s(b).

Each smooth-point blowup changes the intersection of two sections by one
exactly when both pass through the centre. Consequently, for the degree-d
horizontal zero/pole divisors Z0,Pinf of pi,

    I_Y,s(b,Pinf) <= d L_s(b),
    I_Y,s(b,Z0) <= v_s(a)+d L_s(b).

The first uses that integral a and infinity sections are disjoint on the
base and pi is a morphism on Z. The second uses restriction of div(pi)
near b on Z: it is effective there, so its horizontal zero intersection
is <=v_s(a). This explicitly charges collisions with zero at primes |a.

## Vertical-pole bound on the minimal model

Write div_Y(pi)=Z0-Pinf+sum_C v_C C in a fibre at s. The dual graph is
connected, with unit edges and delta_s geometric nodes; loops are harmless.
Intersecting a principal divisor with components makes v solve the graph
Laplacian equation with current vector from Z0-Pinf. Its total positive
current is <=d. Therefore

    max_C v_C-min_C v_C <= d delta_s.

Proof: choose a threshold between the endpoint values of any
edge. All crossing currents have the same sign, so that edge's voltage
drop is at most the total positive source d. Connect extrema by a path
with <=delta_s edges. No inverse spectral-gap estimate is used.

A section meets a smooth point of a regular semistable fibre. Restriction
of div(pi) to b gives

    v_Cb = v_s(a)-I_Y,s(b,Z0)+I_Y,s(b,Pinf) >= -d L_s(b).

Hence m_s(pi)=max(0,-min_C v_C) <=d(L_s(b)+delta_s), and

    V_pi := sum_s m_s(pi)log Norm(s)/[K:Q]
        <= d[h_Z(b)+Delta_st(C)].

Equivalently use u=pi-(a-1), so u(b)=1. Its zeros and b are disjoint on Z,
its poles and negative vertical valuations agree with pi, and the same
graph proof gives the bound without a v_s(a) term. This pays the vertical
term using stable discriminant, without bounding the nonminimal node count.
Z must be the SPECIFIC source normalization-resolution: its finite
div(d pi) identity bounds h_Z(b), not merely h_Y(b). An arbitrary further
blowup is not free. Splitting fields here prove heights only; node subdivision
under base change preserves normalized Delta and crepant canonical heights.

## Removal of book9.1.3's support-etale assumption

On a regular semistable model and a section Q outside the generic zero and
pole supports, restriction of the principal divisor gives

    max(0,-v_s(pi(Q))) <= I_s(Q,Pinf)+m_s(pi).

When pi(Q)=0, its finite coordinate-height contribution is zero and the
inequality holds directly; do not restrict the zero principal function.
Thus collisions between horizontal zero and pole sections do not by
themselves obstruct the finite inequality. At an archimedean place let
G=gr with log-distance singularity, and put

    u(Q)=0.5 log(1+|pi(Q)|²)+G(Pinf,Q),
    H_pi=0.5 integral_C log(1+|pi|²) mu.

The Green representation for dd^c u=pi^*FS-d mu is

    u(Q)=integral_C G(Q,R) pi^*FS(R)+H_pi.

It gives u(Q)<=d sup G+H_pi. Summing the local inequalities is precisely
the book coordinate-height inequality, without demanding disjoint
horizontal supports. The actual source's final identity has this plus sign;
its opposite Laplacian convention does not change the final formula.

## Archimedean moment bound

Use the SAME b above a. The established global lower bound is

    G(b,R)>=log dist_ch(a,pi(R))-log(Cd)-Lambda',

away from equal base images, which form a measure-zero set. Since pi has
degree d and FS has total mass one,

    integral_C log dist_ch(a,pi(R)) pi^*FS(R)=-d/2.

Evaluate the Green identity at b, and use G(Pinf,b)<=d sup G:

    H_pi <= d sup G+0.5 log(1+a²)
              +d[log(Cd)+Lambda'+1/2].

All embedding averages are polynomial in d,hB,log(N+1) by the existing
Merkl bound and the small integer choice of a. No charts need to be
constructed algorithmically for this height inequality.

## Assembly with actual book9.2.5

On Y take D=g b. Arakelov adjunction gives b²=-h_Y(b)[K:Q], hence
-(D,D-omega)/2 = g(g+1)h_Y(b)[K:Q]/2. Dropping the nonnegative
log-cardinality term, the source bounds each (D_t,P) by this term plus
2g² Delta_st, the theta-supremum sum, g log(2pi)/2, half the Faltings
height, and (g b,P). For P over infinity the finite cross-intersection
is <=h_Z(b), and the established global Green lower bound pays its
archimedean part by Lambda'+log(Cd)+0.5 log(1+a²).

Sum this over Pinf with multiplicities (total degree d). Then sum the
coordinate-height inequality over the degree-g divisor D_t itself:

    sum_Q h(pi(Q)) <= (D_t,Pinf)/[K:Q]
                      +g[d sup G_bar+H_pi_bar+V_pi].

Known bounds h_Z(b)<=C_r d³ S_N, Delta_st<=C_r d^6(d+1+hB),
Theta_av<=C_r[d³+d log(d+1+hB)], h_Fal<=C_r d^5(d+1+hB) give the
d^9 S_N envelope. This is not yet a certified reconstruction
algorithm and does not address native frame/good-model constructions.

## Finite support avoidance

For any specified forbidden point P and any class t, D_t contains P iff
H0(K_C tensor t^-1 tensor O(P)) has a section vanishing to order >=g at b.
That space has dimension g and degree 2g-1. Its ordinary Wronskian is
nonzero in characteristic zero (or characteristic>2g-1) and has degree
g(2g-1)+g(g-1)²=g³. Thus at most Ng³ times the number of forbidden
geometric points must be added to the common-basepoint bad set. This
pays avoidance of poles and plane-chart exceptions with small log-height
base values; it must not be invoked in unrestricted characteristic.

The combined bad-basepoint count is at most Ng³(1+d+A), plus r branch
values. Choosing an integer a<=r+Ng³(1+d+A)+1 outside their images ensures
EVERY b above a works; its logarithmic height has the advertised bound.

Status: transfer, graph, moment, assembly and avoidance claims are independently
checked and parent-accepted in the stated scope. Existing input theorems and their
precise sources are in SURFACE_UNIFORM_ARITHMETIC_HEIGHT.md and reviews
surface-theta-delta, merkl-log-atlas, surface-faltings-transfer and book-height-
minimality. Closed divisor encoding, faithful input presentation, and rational
reconstruction remain separate interfaces. No full comparator, speedup or
hardness is inferred.

## Closed-coordinate bridge, independently checked

The full review audits/reviews/2026-11-12-closed-divisor-encoding.md was
parent-read. Let F(x,y)=0 be an absolutely irreducible plane model, x=pi,
total degree D and projective coefficient height H_F, and avoid its at most
D² geometric normalization points outside the affine nonsingular locus.
For E=D_t of degree g put H=sum multiplicity*(h(x)+h(y)). Root heights give

    H <= (D+1) sum multiplicity*h(pi Q)+g[H_F+O(log(D+2))].

For N such divisors one integer 0<=c<=Ng(g+1)/2 makes z=x+c y separate
each support and be a local parameter there. The latter requires
eta=F_y-cF_x nonzero, including at repeated support. There are unique
A monic of degree g and B,C of degree<g with

    K[E]=K[z]/A,    x=B(z), y=C(z),
    h([1,coeff A,coeff B,coeff C])
       <= C_0{DgH+g²[H_F+log max(1,|c|)+log(gD+2)]}.

This encodes the entire nonreduced divisor, not just pi-values. The exact
jet recurrence D_z^n f=P_n/eta^(2n-1), deg P_n<=2nD, and linear-in-n
coefficient height pay inverse tangents. Confluent Vandermonde determinants
pay separation denominators with no collective splitting-field cost.
From a CLOSED divisor algebra construct A by the multiplication matrix of
z, test eta invertibility and cyclicity of 1,z,...,z^(g-1), then solve for
B,C. No support factoring is required.

To turn intrinsic heights into coordinate bits over K, charge BOTH its
degree e and its presentation height B_K. Trace-dual basis bounds give
bit length poly(e,B_K,D,g,H_F,H,log(c+1)). A supplied low-degree field in
an arbitrarily high-height basis is not a paid input. This proves polynomial
intrinsic encoding heights once the plane-model size is paid. It does not
supply the global torsion field, canonical divisor, compatible numerical
lift or Galois-invariant rational reconstruction. Those remain separate.

# Numerical torsion lift from closed divisors

2026-11-12. Scoped classical bridge, independently source-checked in
`audits/reviews/2026-11-12-surface-mascot-lift.md`. This advances the native
surface comparator by paying numerical lifting once a faithful arithmetic
model is available. It does not pay reconstruction precision or that model.

## Exact statement

Given a genus-g curve with good reduction at P, an actual point O, a faithful
separable plane/function-field presentation of its good special curve, and
polynomial-size exact generic Riemann--Roch coordinates, an actual prime-to-P
ell-torsion class represented by closed divisors can be lifted to precision
P^E with polynomial bit cost in the presented sizes, g, numerical E, residue
extension degree, log P and log ell. No geometric support splitting is needed.
This is classical Mascot/Khuri-Makdisi arithmetic; no quantum advantage follows.

For d0=2g+1 and D0=d0 O, a class D-gO becomes D'=D+(d0-g)O,
represented by L(2D0-D'). Closed-place RR constructs this subspace. One common
residue field of polynomial degree supplies more than 5d0 evaluation points
away from denominators and exceptional loci: Hasse--Weil and factoring random
projection fibres give a polynomial capped clock. Unit derivatives lift them
over one unramified local extension. Their supports are independent of D.

Compute exact RR functions in a common-denominator normal form and saturate

Thus the product polynomial and uniquely interpolated tables for **Galois-equivariant operations** have rational coefficients.

This does not require splitting geometric divisor supports. The coefficients of a unique closed divisor lie in its field of definition.

At an auxiliary prime where these fibres are étale, one common residue extension also suffices: the fibre Frobenius orders divide \(s\), while the order on \(E\) divides \(|\operatorname{GL}_R(\mathbf F_\ell)|\). A common extension of degree dividing their product accommodates both. Any additional field used by the admitted lifting implementation remains separately charged.

### The dimension and action conventions

For right deck maps \(R_g\),
\[
A(g)=R_g^*,\qquad P(g)=(R_g)_*=A(g^{-1}).
\]
Here \(A\) is a left representation and \(P\) is a right action. With
\[
S=(\mathbf F_\ell^n)^\vee,\qquad
W=\operatorname{Hom}_\Gamma(S,E),
\]
the admitted natural-socle statement is
\[
\dim W=m,\qquad E\simeq S\otimes W,\qquad \dim E=nm=R.
\]
It is **not** an identification of \(W\) with a collection of actual torsion classes.

The pair set has \(N=s\ell^R\) elements and is not itself the torsion group. For example, legitimate equivariant tables include
\[
((b,t),(c,u))\longmapsto(b,t+u),\qquad
(b,t)\longmapsto(b,0),\qquad
(b,t)\longmapsto(bg,t).
\]
One must subsequently remove the torsor factor, rather than regard all \(N\) labels as \(E\).

None of these repairs supplies target-faithful coordinates.

## 2. Height bounds solve certification—not reduction quality

Grant that every scalar tuple coordinate has absolute logarithmic height at most \(H_0\), including the separately bounded basepoint coordinates.

For a linear functional with \(L\) coordinates and coefficients of absolute value at most \(A\), a safe bound is
\[
h(\gamma(z))\le L(H_0+\log\max(1,A))+\log L=:H_\gamma.
\]
Then, for instance,
\[
h(Q_\gamma)\le N(H_\gamma+\log 2).
\]

Writing
\[
L_i(X)=
\frac{\prod_{j\ne i}(X-\alpha_j)}
     {\prod_{j\ne i}(\alpha_i-\alpha_j)},
\qquad \alpha_i=\gamma(z_i),
\]
gives polynomial height bounds for every coefficient of \(L_i\). Unary tables use \(N\) such terms; binary tables use \(N^2\). Their coefficient heights consequently remain polynomial in \(N,L,H_0,\log A\).

The degree bound \(D\) also bounds local valuations of nonzero algebraic differences. Together these bounds support certified precision propagation and rational reconstruction, rather than an integer-relation guess. All lifting, interpolation, rational arithmetic and output sizes must still be charged.

But
\[
\text{a polynomial bound on }h(Q_\gamma)
\quad\not\Rightarrow\quad
p\nmid\operatorname{disc}(Q_\gamma).
\]
A height bound pays for a denominator or discriminant; it does not make it a \(p\)-adic unit.

## 3. Counterexample: all candidate functionals fail at \(p\)

Start with an admissible canonical encoding. Denote its torsion-dependent scalar entries by
\[
u_1(b,t),\ldots,u_L(b,t).
\]
They determine the same actual closed divisors as before. Suppose their heights are bounded by \(H_0\).

Every such entry has algebraic degree at most \(D\). For every place above \(p\), using \(v_p(p)=1\),
\[
v_p(u_j)\ge-\frac{D H_0}{\log p}
\]
when \(u_j\ne0\).

Choose the explicitly bounded integer
\[
k=1+\left\lceil\frac{D H_0}{\log p}\right\rceil
\]
and replace the encoding by
\[
u'_j(b,t)=p^k u_j(b,t).
\]
Leave any torsion-independent basepoint entries unchanged. Any torsion-dependent chart tags can be encoded with the same scaling.

This is an invertible, explicitly known rational reencoding. Its inverse divides by the known integer \(p^k\); no number field or Galois advice is needed.

### It preserves the admitted promises

- The genuine cover, evaluation, torsion classes and \(h^0=1\) assertions are unchanged.
- It remains Galois-equivariant.
- At \(P\ne p\), multiplication by \(p^k\) is a unit. Thus faithful small-\(P\) encoding and lifting are unchanged.
- The height increase is polynomial:
  \[
  h(u'_j)\le H_0+k\log p
  \le H_0+D H_0+2\log p.
  \]
- The scaling and its inverse have polynomial bit size.
- No new characteristic-zero chart exception is introduced.

Thus it satisfies the stated *type* of encoding-height interface. If “canonical” is intended to forbid this reencoding, the missing restriction must be stated as an integral normalization property; uniqueness and a height bound do not imply it.

### Every integer functional collides

For every \(j,b,t\),
\[
u'_j(b,t)\in p\mathcal O_{\overline{\mathbf Q}_p}.
\]
Hence, for a fixed \(b\) and any \(t,t'\in E\), every integer linear functional satisfies
\[
\gamma(\operatorname{enc}'(b,t))
-
\gamma(\operatorname{enc}'(b,t'))
\in p\mathcal O_{\overline{\mathbf Q}_p}.
\]

Therefore:

- either \(Q_\gamma\) is not \(p\)-integral, so direct reduction is unavailable;
- or its roots are integral and the \(M=\ell^R>1\) labels over each fixed \(b\) have the same reduction.

In the second case, over \(\overline{\mathbf F}_p\),
\[
\overline{Q_\gamma}(X)
  =\prod_{b\in T_a}(X-c_b)^M,
\]
possibly with further coincidences among the \(c_b\). It is never squarefree.

This applies to **every** integer coefficient vector, not merely a particular moment curve or a finite candidate grid. Moving \(b\) does not help: the collision occurs among the torsion labels over each \(b\). In fact, any integral polynomial functional of these entries has the same problem.

The elementary two-label illustration is
\[
Q(X)=X(X-p).
\]
It is separable over \(\mathbf Q\), has small logarithmic height, and is perfectly usable at an auxiliary \(P\ne p\). But
\[
\overline Q=X^2.
\]
Applying \(X\mapsto X^p\) to this nonreduced order is not the arithmetic permutation of the two characteristic-zero labels.

### This is not a finite-small-\(p\) issue

The construction works for arbitrarily large \(p\). Its coefficients depend on \(p\), with logarithmic size \(O(B)\), exactly as the interface permits.

Thus
\[
p>\text{every relevant fixed polynomial in }\ell
\]
does not repair it. One cannot appeal to “only finitely many bad primes for a fixed encoding” when the native instance and its encoding vary with the target prime.

## 4. The exact missing success lemma

A direct-reduction algorithm needs an effective statement of the following form.

> **Target-faithful selector.** There is a polynomial-size, polynomial-bit candidate family of fibres and encoding charts, with a computable bound, such that at least one candidate is admissible at \(P\), has an unramified target fibre, and gives a \(p\)-integral tuple encoding that separates every pair after reduction.

“Finite chart exceptions in characteristic zero” is insufficient. The selector needs a bound on the bad locus **after reduction at \(p\)** and a proof that it is not the whole parameter space.

Once a target-faithful tuple exists, the remaining functional search is elementary. For
\[
\gamma_c(z)=\sum_{j=0}^{L-1}c^jz_j,
\]
each pair excludes at most \(L-1\) values of \(c\), so at most
\[
C_\gamma=(L-1)\binom N2
\]
values are bad. If \(p>C_\gamma\), testing \(C_\gamma+1\) distinct residues guarantees success.

The missing premise is that each pair’s difference polynomial is nonzero modulo \(p\). The counterexample makes those polynomials identically zero.

### Verification is available; guaranteed success is not

For a reconstructed candidate, the following are exact, polynomial-size checks:

1. the required rational denominators are prime to \(p\);
2. \(\gcd(\overline Q_\gamma,\overline Q_\gamma')=1\);
3. the reduced operation tables satisfy the required identities;
4. the selected frame fibre has the required target étaleness.

These use division by the known prime \(p\) and finite-field arithmetic, not factorization of a target-sized integer.

They certify a successful candidate. They do **not** establish that a bounded search contains one. In the counterexample, every candidate correctly fails.

For \(p\le C_\gamma\), a complete algorithm also needs an explicitly charged alternative to a single primitive coordinate; it cannot silently discard those cases.

## 5. What a repair would have to pay

A different algorithm could avoid target-good divisor charts by:

1. reconstructing the rational finite algebra and operations;
2. taking the quotient corresponding to \(E\);
3. computing a \(p\)-maximal, finite-étale order using the promised unramified representation;
4. reducing that order and computing its Frobenius.

That is a plausible algorithmic repair, not supplied global advice. But its construction, polynomial bit bounds, operation-table transport and output extraction must be proved and charged. Merely invoking good reduction does not make the initially reconstructed monogenic order \(p\)-maximal.

If either repair succeeds, the full-frame conventions then give
\[
\phi g^T=P(g)\phi,\qquad
F_W(\phi)=F_E\circ\phi.
\]
Under the supplied arithmetic identification, the corrections are \(p^{-1}\) for \(H^1(U,L)\) and \(p^{-2}\) for the stated untwisted coefficient system; geometric Frobenius is the inverse.

**Bottom line:** all-pairs orbit encoding repairs the algebraic-basepoint and global-field problems, and **[Height]** can repair heuristic reconstruction. It does not supply a target-faithful reduction. The proposed integer-\(\gamma\)/basepoint search has a counterexample under the written interfaces.
